kind: MuJoCo simulation; not real robot evidence

protocol.transport: One simulation clock. 20ms captures. Constant 40ms delay in delay-40ms. Every third post-fault packet delayed 80ms in reordered. Gap suppresses delivery during [4.8,5.04); no catch-up. Stale-replay delivers the last pre-gap good packet until 5.2. gap-and-drop also opens the gripper during [4.8,5.04).
protocol.recovery: Hold retains actuator targets, physics continues. Revalidate requires unique, ordered, post-hold captures, age <60ms, bilateral contact, cube_z >0.12m and cube-to-grip distance <0.05m, spanning100ms with gaps<=20ms. At600ms abort takes precedence. Replan from current measured grip pose to original transfer destination, followed by original lower/release/retreat/settle. Receipt baseline resumes the wall-clock trajectory after any valid packet, including stale/duplicate. Latched never resumes.
protocol.hypothesis: New deliveries alone can produce unsafe resume decisions. Post-hold state evidence plus a new path can separate harmless communication gaps from lost grasps.
protocol.scope: 18 deterministic rollouts, one per cell. Privileged simulated observations, no learned policy, physical robot, real network or clock skew. Policies are bundles; differences do not isolate individual components. Synthetic fault schedules; no probabilistic success rate.
